text: Corner singularities, curved coordinates and Neumann/Robin boundaries Actually solve singular L-corner P1 FEM, annular variable-viscosity vector Q1 PDE, pure-Neumann compatibility/mean-gauge and mixed-Robin manufactured problems. These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-mesh-boundary-2026-11-23 from the ZIP. This command executes all 4 fixed cases in the supplement. Choose a new or empty output directory. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. L-corner P1 FEM: grading and separate mesh distortion Solve a harmonic reentrant-corner field with actual2D P1 FEM; compare matched-DOF uniform/grading and separate smooth-square mesh distortion. Methods, equations, figures and references Input and validation protocol history · Initial input Assumptions, units and boundaries L-shaped[-1,1]² minus quadrantIV, theta0..3pi/2, analytic Dirichlet harmonic corner field. N8/16/32, fixed map x→x max(|x|,|y|). Separate unit-square sine MMS uses regular/warped grids. Editorial clarification No smooth-square L2 order is imposed on the singular field. Fixed a-priori grading is not an AMR engine. Conditioning is estimated; arbitrary distortion is not certified. Adopted numerical method Assemble physical P1 gradients/areas, eliminate boundary data and solve sparse systems. Interactive FEM: graded meshes around vertex singularities Review scope / review_level: selected-author-teaching-section Annular variable-viscosity vector PDE MMS Actually solve variable-viscosity stress divergence on an annulus; check velocity, strain, physical traction and work. Methods, equations, figures and references Input and validation protocol history · Initial input Assumptions, units and boundaries 1≤r≤2, periodic angle, mu=1+.2r², lambda0 and zero velocity on both circles. A(s)=(s−1)(4−s), u=(A(1+xy),A(x²−y²)/2). Nr8/16/32,Ntheta2Nr. Editorial clarification A linear vector viscous BVP, without divergence-free constraint, pressure or nonlinear Navier–Stokes. r>0 only; no axis stencil certification. Adopted numerical method Mapped polar Q1 with two Cartesian velocity components;4×4 Gauss integration of2mu epsilon uses exact r dr dtheta metric, followed by a block sparse solve. Circular traction uses r dtheta and outward normals. −∇⋅(2μϵ(u))=f,μ=1+0.2r2−∇⋅(2μϵ(u))=f,μ=1+0.2r2 ∫2μϵ(u):ϵ(v) r dr dθ=∫f⋅v r dr dθ∫2μϵ(u):ϵ(v)rdrdθ=∫f⋅vrdrdθ dS=r dθ,t=(2μϵ(u))ndS=rdθ,t=(2μϵ(u))n References and measured quantities Qualify the derived force by separate Cartesian stress differentiation.
